$comment:
Array-items part-default case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an
OpenAPI form request body: openbindings-go/formats/openapi, openapi-client/go, and
openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi re-exports). Each case is
rendered as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and loaded through the engine's own loader, so the table
exercises the shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model.

WHAT THIS TABLE GUARDS. Every accepted OAS edition derives an ARRAY property's default
`contentType` from its ITEMS schema, never from the array itself:

  3.0.0-3.0.3, 3.1.0  'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'
  3.0.4               'array | n/a | according to the type and format of the items schema'
  3.1.1, 3.1.2        'array | n/a | according to the type of the items schema'

The three engines hold that invariant on the multipart lane by reducing an array property to its
items schema before the per-type default is consulted, in BOTH the media-admission lane and the
body-encoding lane. Until this table existed, nothing asserted it: deleting the reduction turned
no test red. That is what the multipart cells are for.

Two independent sentences say it, and they are complementary: the Encoding Object row above
appears in every edition, and the multipart guidance in 3.0.0-3.0.3 and 3.1.0 - exactly the five
editions whose row says 'inner type' - adds 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of
primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain' and 'If the property is complex, or an
array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'. Counted against the
pinned edition texts with corpus-lab/scripts/strip-oas-html.mjs: 1/1/1/1/0/1/0/0.

Multiplicity is NOT this table's claim. OAS 3.0.4 / 3.1.1 / 3.1.2 state 'Array properties are
handled by applying the same name to multiple parts, as is recommended by [RFC7578] Section 4'
(count 0/0/0/0/1/0/1/1) and 3.1.0 says 'each schema property, or each element of a schema array
property, takes a section in the payload with an internal header as defined by [RFC7578]' (count
0/0/0/0/0/1/0/0). OAS 3.0.0-3.0.3 state neither, and the repeated-part expansion those four
editions get is the implementations' pre-existing convention. The table pins the expansion as it
stands rather than deriving it.

THE URLENCODED CONTENT LANE IS AN OPEN CELL, PINNED AS OBSERVED, NOT AS AUTHORITY. On 3.0.4 and
the 3.1 line an urlencoded property with no Encoding Object takes the content path, and there the
engines derive an array property's default from the ARRAY (application/json) rather than from its
items schema. Those cells carry basis 'OPEN' and record the emission as it stands today, so that
a future change to them has to be a deliberate edit of this table. The cell is filed in
corpus-lab/OPENAPI-RUNTIME.md under 'The array-items part default'; it is entangled with the
pending 3.0-line lane question in design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md, because a
ruling that moves 3.0.0-3.0.3 onto the content machine moves those properties into this same
cell. Nothing here prejudges either question.

DECISION FORMAT, identical in all three engines. 'refused' means the request-body plan refuses
the candidate before any value is supplied. Otherwise 'admitted;emit=<rendering>', where the
rendering is:
  multipart   each emitted part as '<Content-Type>:<body>', joined by '&', in emission order;
              'elided' when no part is emitted; 'error' when the encoder refuses the value.
              A part with NO Content-Type header renders as 'text/plain:', because [RFC7578]
              Section 4.4 says 'Each part MAY have an (optional) "Content-Type" header field,
              which defaults to "text/plain"' - so emitting the header and omitting it are the
              same wire fact and both are inside the permitted set. The Go engines emit it; the
              TypeScript engine, which builds parts through FormData, omits it for a plain text
              field. Requiring either spelling would invent a preference no authority states.
              Content-Transfer-Encoding is outside the rendering for the same reason of
              expressibility: TypeScript inserts it after FormData has serialized, so a twin
              table cannot compare it. It is pinned by each engine's own tests.
  urlencoded  the whole emitted body; 'elided' when empty; 'error' when the encoder refuses.

Refusal MESSAGES are each implementation's own surface and are never compared.

THE WRITE LANE REFUSES WHAT THE ADMISSION LANE REFUSES. A multipart nested-array cell is refused by the media-admission lane, so no plan carrying that declaration can be selected and the body-encoding lane is unreachable for it on the wire. It was not unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION: the encoder expanded the declaration anyway and emitted one application/json part per element. The `writeLane` field pins the encoder's own decision for those cells, measured by calling the body-encoding entry point directly rather than through admission, so the two lanes are asserted to agree about one declaration instead of one lane being asserted and the other trusted. Refusal MESSAGES stay each engine's own surface; only the decision crosses the twin boundary.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|string
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is a string with no binary signal, so the applicable row is 'for other primitive types - text/plain'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|integer
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is an integer, so the applicable row is 'for other primitive types - text/plain'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|object
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is an object, so the applicable row is 'for object - application/json'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|nested-array
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is itself an array, so the row recurses with no base case, and no accepted edition states how the members of an inner array map onto one part name. Deciding that would be authorship rather than incorporation, so the candidate refuses before dispatch (deference order rung 4).

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|unconstrained
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. An unconstrained items schema asserts nothing. The 3.0 line's own list has no row for a schema with no type, and this candidate defines no JSON-to-octet boundary for a declaration that made no claim, so `openbindings.openapi@1` §9.2's stated convention applies: the supplied value's JSON application type supplies the corresponding OAS per-type default, per element.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|string-base64
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. `contentEncoding` is not a keyword of the 3.0 Schema Object's dialect - the 3.0 binary signal is `format` - so the applicable row is the one for a string with no binary format, and the annotation carries no content-encoding force.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|union-type
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. Every 3.0 edition states of the Schema Object: 'type - Value MUST be a string. Multiple types via an array are not supported.' An array-valued `type` is therefore not a union declaration on this line and no part carriage follows from one.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|union-choice
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema declares a choice with more than one non-null branch, which `openbindings.openapi@1` §9.2 refuses: it declares value-dependent alternatives and leaves no single faithful form carriage.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|string
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.0-3.0.3 apply the Encoding Object's serialization defaults to every urlencoded property: `style` follows the Parameter Object's query default `form`, and `explode` 'when style is form, the default value is true'. The content-based interpretation first appears in 3.0.4, so on this edition the property takes the style path and the contentType default table is not consulted at all - which is why the items schema does not change the emission here.
